questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to stay in Europe because of the Erasmus grant, and I thought Lisbon was the most “exotic” destination Europe has to offer. The warm climate, with summer lasting until November, was very appealing. Additionally, I really wanted to learn how to surf. I chose my destination primarily based on the lifestyle and activities available rather than academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. As long as you remember to check your email, you will receive all the necessary information from both KU and NOVA.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance upon arrival. However, NOVA had an Erasmus Student Center help desk where students could get support with study-related questions, for example if they experienced issues with course registration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was fairly easy to find off-campus housing. We found our accommodation through
Uniplaces.com
, which worked very well. They charge a service fee, but it is worth it, as they verify landlords and significantly reduce the risk of scams.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
NOVA University is located in Carcavelos, right by the beach. While some students choose to live nearby, I would strongly recommend living in Lisbon instead, as there is not much to do in Carcavelos besides studying and going to the beach.

If you live in Lisbon, it is important to make sure that your accommodation has easy access to the train. Areas such as Santos or Cais do Sodré are good options, as you can reach the university in about 40 minutes, which is very manageable.

Be careful about travel time when choosing housing. In my first accommodation, the commute was almost one and a half hours each way, which quickly becomes exhausting and takes up a lot of free time. Always check Google Maps in advance to ensure that you can reach NOVA easily.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Rent is more or less at Copenhagen price levels (around 5,000 DKK or more per month). However, there are also shared flats available on Uniplaces, which tend to be slightly cheaper.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
NOVA divides course registration into two rounds.

In the first round, registration is not first-come, first-served. Students submit their course preferences, and places are assigned randomly. I was fortunate to receive almost all of my preferred courses in this round, although some students only received a few.

The second round is first-come, first-served. NOVA sends an email in advance with information about when registration opens, and it is important to be ready at that time. I did not get my remaining courses immediately, but persistence helped, as places continued to open up. The second round was open for approximately two to three days.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
There was limited formal assistance available. Most of the helpful information came from earlier Erasmus students who shared their experiences.

I was concerned about not getting the courses I wanted and contacted NOVA by email. However, there was not much they could do, and the only option was to register during the second registration round. In the end, everything worked out, and I was able to enroll in all of my courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all of my preferred classes. Almost everyone I know also ended up getting the courses they wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not give up during the second registration round. Check the registration page frequently, as spots may open up during the two to three days of the registration period.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses were below the academic level at UCPH. Only Advanced Microeconomics was equivalent to the level we are familiar with from home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Lectures were much smaller, typically with around 30 students per lecture.

Practical classes were also different, as students did not work independently on exercises. Instead, the instructor went through examples.

There was more structured and mandatory activity, such as class presentations, which made the teaching style feel more similar to a Danish high school than to UCPH. However, the atmosphere was relaxed, and attendance was generally not registered, except for tests or presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Microeconomics, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as Micro III)
Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History, 3.5 ECTS (pre-approved as Economic History together with Economic History)
Economic History, 3.5 ECTS (pre-approved as Economic History together with Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History)
Development Economics, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as Development Economics)
International Trade, 7 ECTS (pre-approved as International Economics)
Ethics, 3.5 ECTS (taken to fulfill the 30 ECTS requirement)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend Advanced Microeconomics! I have generally not enjoyed microeconomics courses in Denmark, but the professor teaching this course at NOVA (Paulo) was excellent. The course is pre-approved as Micro III (Game Theory), but it covers material from Micro I, Micro II, and Micro III. The academic level is comparable to UCPH, and the lectures are very well structured, with clear and intuitive examples that made the material easier to understand.

I also enjoyed the two history courses, Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History and Economic History. Both courses must be taken together in order to receive approval as Økonomisk Historie. Although I did not attend many lectures, I found the course readings very interesting, especially for students with an interest in history.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
NOVA has a fitness center on campus, although I did not personally use it. Also, the student club Mindspace organized activities such as yoga and pilates classes held at the beach for approximately 3–6 euros per session.

There is also a surf school called Lisbon Surf Camp located at Carcavelos beach, about a 15-minute walk from the university if you follow the beach. While it is not officially part of NOVA, they offer special deals for Erasmus and NOVA students. For around 50 euros per month, students can get four surf lessons and eight equipment rentals, which is very affordable. The staff was extremely welcoming, and they also organized a surf trip to southern Portugal in November, which was a great experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend trips with friends and surf:) Watch the sunset from one of the many miradouros (viewpoints) in the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
If you surf, Ericeira and Peniche are great destinations, and I would strongly recommend joining the surf trip organized by Lisbon Surf Camp. If you have travel insurance through a credit card, it is often possible to rent a car for as little as around 5 euros per day, which makes road trips with friends very accessible.

Beyond surfing, there are many other experiences to enjoy. A weekend trip to Madeira for hiking is highly recommended, as the nature is absolutely stunning. Porto is also easy to visit from Lisbon by FlixBus. And go to Sintra and beach Ursa. Also, a trip to Nazaré to see the world’s largest waves (often over 20 meters) and the surfers riding them is a must.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy:)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly socialized with other Danish students, as NOVA has a large international student population. At the master’s level, almost half of the students are non-Portuguese, which means that many social activities naturally take place in international groups rather than with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The great weather and the amazing food (especially fish and other seafood).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Academically, the workload is manageable, so I would encourage students to prioritize making the most of their exchange experience. Take advantage of opportunities to travel, surf, and enjoy life outside the classroom, even if that occasionally means missing lectures.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think, I covered the most:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having a lot of fun with great people. Lisbon is amazing!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: no challenges:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
